**Part A — Examples of Conditional Statements**

**Example A**
```{r}
score <- 74

if (score >= 75) {
  print("Passed")
} else {
  print("Failed")
}

```

**Example b**
```{r}
score <- 91

if (score >= 90) {
  print("Excellent")
} else if (score >= 80) {
  print("Good")
} else if (score >= 75) {
  print("Fair")
} else {
  print("Needs Improvement")
}

```

**Example c**
```{r}
scores <- c(92, 68, 75, 81, 59)
ifelse(scores >= 75, "Passed", "Failed")

```

**Example d**
```{r}
grade <- 91
attendance <- 95

if (grade >= 90 & attendance >= 90) {
  print("Honors candidate")
}

```


**Part B — Conditional Statements**

**Question #1**

```{r}
temp <- 33
if (temp >= 32) {
  print("Hot")
} else {
  print("Not hot")
}
```

**Question #2**

```{r}
age <- 17
if (age < 13) {
  print("Child")
} else if (age <= 19) {
  print("Teenager")
} else {
  print("Adult")
}
```

**Question #3**

```{r}
marks <- c(45, 88, 73, 100, 62)
result <- ifelse(marks >= 60, "Pass", "Fail")
print(result)
```

**Question #4**

```{r}
x <- 10
if (x > 5) {
  print("A")
} else if (x > 8) {
  print("B")
} else {
  print("C")
}

# R checks from top to bottom and stops at the first TRUE condition. x > 5 is TRUE, so "A" prints and the other branches are skipped, even though x > 8 is also TRUE.

```

**Question #5**

What is the difference between if and ifelse()? When would you choose each one?

if works on one value, while ifelse() works on a whole vector. Use if for single decisions and ifelse() for columns.

grades$FinalGrade

**f.2**

```{r}
grades$Result <- ifelse(is.na(grades$FinalGrade), "Incomplete",
                 ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 75, "Passed", "Failed"))
grades$Result 
```

**f.3**

```{r}
grades$Remarks <- ifelse(is.na(grades$FinalGrade), "Incomplete",
                  ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 90, "Excellent",
                  ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 85, "Very Good",
                  ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 80, "Good",
                  ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 75, "Fair", "Needs Improvement")))))
grades$Remarks 
```

**f.4**

```{r}
grades$AttendanceFlag <- ifelse(grades$Attendance < 80, "At Risk", "OK")
grades$AttendanceFlag 
```

**f.5** 

```{r}
grades$Honors <- ifelse(!is.na(grades$FinalGrade) &
                        grades$FinalGrade >= 90 &
                        grades$Attendance >= 90, "Yes", "No")
grades$Honors 
```

**f.6**

```{r}
result_loop <- character(nrow(grades))

for (i in 1:nrow(grades)) {
  if (is.na(grades$FinalGrade[i])) {
    result_loop[i] <- "Incomplete"
  } else if (grades$FinalGrade[i] >= 75) {
    result_loop[i] <- "Passed"
  } else {
    result_loop[i] <- "Failed"
  }
}
result_loop
```

**Part D: Exporting Results**

**Question #7**

```{r}
#a 
write.csv(grades, "students_grades_processed.csv", row.names = FALSE)

#b
at_risk <- grades[grades$AttendanceFlag == "At Risk", ]
if (nrow(at_risk) > 0) {
  write.csv(at_risk, "at_risk_students.csv", row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  print("No at-risk students.")
}

#c 
honors <- grades[grades$Honors == "Yes",
                 c("StudentID", "Name", "Section", "FinalGrade", "Attendance")]
if (nrow(honors) > 0) {
  write.csv(honors, "honors_list.csv", row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  print("No honors candidates.")
}

#d
check <- read.csv("students_grades_processed.csv")
dim(check)                          
head(check)
all.equal(check$FinalGrade, grades$FinalGrade)
```


**Question #8**

```{r}
write.csv(grades, "temp_test.csv")
head(read.csv("temp_test.csv"))
```
1. How does the missing midterm appear in the exported file?

It shows up as NA in the file. Use na = "" if you want the cell left empty.

2. What would the file look like without row.names = FALSE? Try it with a temporary file name and compare.

Without row.names = FALSE, the file gets an extra numbering column, which shows up as X when read back.


**Question #9**

```{r}
grades$Scholarship <- ifelse(is.na(grades$FinalGrade), "Pending",
                      ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 95 & grades$Attendance >= 90, "Full",
                      ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 85 & grades$Attendance >= 90, "Partial",
                             "None")))
```

```{r}
qualified <- grades[grades$Scholarship %in% c("Full", "Partial"), ]

```

```{r}
if (nrow(qualified) > 0) {
  write.csv(qualified, "scholarship_candidates.csv", row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  print("No scholarship candidates.")
}
qualified 
```

```{r}
table(grades$Scholarship)
```

**Question #10**

```{r}
# 1. Comparing anything with NA gives NA, and if() can't decide on NA. Checking is.na() first avoids the error.

# 2. The student with a missing grade would get NA instead of "Incomplete". Incomplete must come first so the NA is caught before any comparison.

# 3. Use ifelse() to fill a whole column. Use if ... else for a single decision, like checking whether a file exists.

# 4. It shows the file was saved correctly: right rows and columns, no extra numbering column, and NA saved as expected.

```
